messages:
rei: flagging weird OOM pattern on aurora-13b int8 canary. only on long multi-turn sessions (>3k tokens). batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=180.
sam: thanks. allocation traces?
rei: paste: ```CUDA OOM during alloc
GPU total: 80GB, highwater: 78.9GB, free: 1.1GB
KV cache estimate: 65GB
Small slab fragments: 1103 (<48KB)
Req tokens (history+gen): 3180
Batch:4, max_new_tokens:180```
priya: sounds like slab fragmentation from altered int8 buffer alignment. can we try two quick mitigations: lower max_new_tokens to 96 and enable microbatching for requests with context_estimate>2500?
sam: microbatching would serialize generation per item which reduces simultaneous KV peaks. perf cost expected ~5% p50, p95 up more. worth it to stop OOMs in hosted.
rei: ran a 2k-request synthetic: microbatch + max_new_tokens=96 dropped frag_index 0.39 -> 0.16 and eliminated OOMs. latency p95 +12% on the longest requests. quality diffs minimal on our short-summary eval, but long-summary ROUGE-L -0.7 vs fp16.
priya: routing idea: add per-route tag `quality_sensitive` and prefer fp16 for those routes (e.g., /v1/summarize/long). default remains int8. also add soft_truncate_when_context>3200 to protect allocator.
sam: agreed. rollout plan: 1) canary flags: max_new_tokens=96, microbatch=on, soft_truncate=on 2) tag long-summary routes as quality_sensitive -> prefer fp16 3) 48h soak w/ mixed prompts 4) alerts: OOM_rate>0.02% OR ROUGE-L drop>0.5 -> rollback or route-fallback.
ops-bot: canary queued: aurora-13b:int8 flags=[max_new_tokens=96,microbatch=on,soft_truncate=on]; target=eng-staging; started=2026-03-28T14:00Z
rei: thanks all. opening PR with config diffs and eval snapshot. will monitor frag metrics and route-fallback counts. :white_check_mark:
